cards.title: The Olympic Games Once Awarded Medals for Fine Arts
cards.body: Between 1912 and 1948, the Olympic Games awarded official medals in fine arts alongside athletic events. Inspired by Pierre de Coubertin's vision of uniting mind and body, contestants submitted original works in architecture, literature, music, painting, and sculpture, all themed around sport. The competitions were discontinued after 1948 because the vast majority of participating artists were professionals, violating the era's strict amateurism rules.

cards.title: Fire Preserved the World's Oldest Royal Library
cards.body: In the 7th century BCE, Neo-Assyrian king Ashurbanipal assembled an immense systematic library at Nineveh in modern-day Iraq. His scribes gathered over 30,000 cuneiform clay tablets covering medicine, astronomy, state treaties, and the Epic of Gilgamesh. When invaders torched the royal palace in 612 BCE, the catastrophic fire did not destroy the collection—it baked and hardened the clay tablets, preserving them for modern archaeologists.

cards.title: Pirate Ships Ran on Radical Workplace Democracy
cards.body: During the Golden Age of Piracy, crews operated under written constitutions known as Articles of Agreement. Crew members elected their captains and quartermasters by popular vote, could depose tyrannical leaders, and divided captured plunder through strict share systems. Decades before modern welfare states, pirate agreements even established formal workers' compensation schemes that paid fixed indemnities for lost eyes, fingers, and limbs.

cards.title: The Loudest Sound in History Circled Earth Four Times
cards.body: When the volcanic island of Krakatoa exploded in August 1883, the blast produced the loudest sound recorded in human history. The detonation ruptured the eardrums of sailors 40 miles away and was heard clearly on Rodrigues Island in the Indian Ocean, nearly 3,000 miles away. The resulting atmospheric shock wave rippled across the globe four times before fading.

cards.title: America's Largest Armed Labor Uprising Was Fought in 1921
cards.body: The largest armed insurrection in the United States since the Civil War occurred at Blair Mountain, West Virginia, in late summer 1921. Approximately 10,000 striking coal miners fought against 3,000 armed deputies, state police, and coal company guards. The week-long battle involved machine guns, fortified ridges, and private planes dropping surplus World War I bombs until federal troops stepped in.

quizzes.question: Why did the International Olympic Committee drop art competitions after 1948?
options: Most artists were professionals, conflicting with amateurism rules
Public attendance at art exhibits fell to zero
Too many sculptures were damaged during overseas shipment
No artist met the entry deadlines for the 1952 Games
quizzes.explanation: Olympic rules at the time strictly required competitors to be amateurs, but nearly all participating artists made their living from art.

quizzes.question: How did the Library of Ashurbanipal survive the sack of Nineveh in 612 BCE?
options: The palace fire baked and hardened the clay tablets
Scribes hid the scrolls in waterproof copper canisters
The collection was buried under deep desert permafrost
Invaders spared the tablets to sell them as currency
quizzes.explanation: Because the texts were inscribed on moist clay tablets, the raging palace fire effectively fired and preserved them.

quizzes.question: How were captains typically selected on 18th-century pirate ships?
options: Elected by a democratic vote of the entire crew
Appointed by wealthy private merchant investors
Inherited through royal letters of marque
Determined by single-combat sword duels
quizzes.explanation: Pirate crews governed themselves democratically, electing their officers and reserving the right to vote them out of office.

quizzes.question: How far away was the sound of the 1883 Krakatoa eruption heard?
options: Nearly 3,000 miles (4,800 km) away
Roughly 250 miles (400 km) away
Only within 50 miles (80 km) of the island
Across every continent on Earth simultaneously
quizzes.explanation: The explosion was loud enough to be heard clearly 2,968 miles away on Rodrigues Island in the western Indian Ocean.

quizzes.question: What triggered the 1921 Battle of Blair Mountain?
options: Striking coal miners fighting armed deputies for union recognition
A border dispute between Virginia and West Virginia militias
Rival railroad barons battling over right-of-way tracks
Farmers protesting federal grain taxation policies
quizzes.explanation: Roughly 10,000 union miners marched to liberate jailed colleagues and unionize southern West Virginia coalfields.

guesses.prompt: How many clay tablets and fragments were preserved in the Library of Ashurbanipal?
guesses.explanation: Over 30,000 cuneiform tablets and fragments survived in the ruins of Nineveh, forming our richest window into ancient Mesopotamia.

guesses.prompt: How many miles away was the sound of Krakatoa's 1883 explosion heard by human ears?
guesses.explanation: The blast traveled nearly 3,000 miles across the Indian Ocean to Rodrigues Island, covering roughly 8% of Earth's surface.

misconceptions.claim: The Olympic Games have only ever awarded medals for athletic physical contests.
misconceptions.explanation: From 1912 to 1948, the Olympic Games awarded 151 official medals for fine arts like painting, sculpture, and music.

misconceptions.claim: Golden Age pirate ships were lawless dictatorships ruled by the strongest fighter.
misconceptions.explanation: Most pirate crews operated under written democratic constitutions that mandated equal voting rights and workplace injury pay.
